findings.text: When process.chdir is disabled (worker threads), the directory change silently fails but which.sync() still runs in the wrong directory. The path.resolve() fix at line 106 is ineffective because which.sync() returns an absolute path, causing file resolution to search the wrong directory.
Shebang parsing with #!/usr/bin/env only captures the first argument after env. A shebang like #!/usr/bin/env node --flag --other would lose '--other', running the wrong interpreter command.
Shebang parsing splits on spaces without handling quotes. A shebang like #!/bin/sh -c 'echo test' would incorrectly parse the quoted argument as multiple tokens, breaking the interpreter command.

0.reason: The code explicitly handles the case where process.chdir is unavailable or disabled, and the path.resolve() call correctly combines the absolute path from which.sync() with the cwd, so the described failure does not occur.

1.reason: This finding describes the same root cause as the reference bug: parseShebang only captures the first argument after env, ignoring additional arguments, which is the same mechanism of losing parts of the shebang line.

2.reason: This finding also describes the same root cause as the reference bug: parseShebang splits on spaces without handling quotes, which is the same mechanism of incorrectly parsing the shebang line.
